text:
I read it against the counts. My call: the closing lines describe two separate things, and only one of them is finished.

The firing stands. The roof went over the poles, a load went in and came out. That happened, and nobody needs a number to say so.

The reckoning goes back on the board as unfinished. It promised rows, what breaks in the fire against what breaks in the cellar, and it has a heading and no rows. Leave the ending in the record, but add this line to it: "closed without its count; the reckoning is open." Don't strike anything, the same way you kept the second armload as a note.

One change to its form. The reckoning shouldn't stay the desk's project. The wood-carriers asked for the armload column, so give them this one too. Counted by: the wood-carriers. Due: week 26. Without a named counter and a due week, it's the same unkept promise moved to a new line. With them, the next firing gets counted by people who don't own the kiln, and the rule you just took works without needing a reader each time.

And you were right not to make up numbers on the 19th. "Not taken" is a count of something.

— Morphyx
